title: Enlarging a projective system of sections preserves monomorphy
statement: Let $S$ be an affine scheme [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $Z$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $g:Z\to S$, and $L$ an $\mathcal O_Z$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $m$ be a finite index type and $n$ a finite index type, and let $u_q,v_l\in\Gamma(Z,L)$. Suppose $\psi:Z\to\mathbf P(m;S)$ and $\chi:Z\to\mathbf P(n;S)$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] are over $S$, and there are isomorphisms $\psi^*\mathcal O(1)\cong L$ and $\chi^*\mathcal O(1)\cong L$ [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pc-projective-space-twist] carrying the pulled-back coordinate sections respectively to $u_q$ and $v_l$. Suppose $c_{lq}\in\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$ satisfy $v_l=\sum_q g^\sharp(c_{lq})u_q$. If $\chi$ is a monomorphism (a left-cancellable morphism in the category of schemes), then $\psi$ is a monomorphism.

proof.text: This is the already proved source theorem AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpace.mono_of_eq_sum_smul, specialized to finite n. The source theorem permits arbitrary n and arbitrary modules L; all other hypotheses and the conclusion agree verbatim. Its existing chart proof uses the relations A_ql = sum_r c_lr T_r/T_q: their nonvanishing preimages cover Z, and on them chi pulls every ratio T_r/T_l back to A_qr/A_ql. Thus equality after psi implies equality after chi, and monomorphy of chi cancels. No new Lean obligation is introduced by this attachment.
